followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the included Enguri H1N1 ordinary-departure interruption with scoped first restoration, not the distinct South Ossetian episode. Ordinary departures from Abkhazia are affected; return entry, medical travel, HPP workers and visa holders have recorded exceptions. Neither both-way total closure nor an unrestricted February restoration is claimed. Retain 10–11 January to 5 February 2019, 25–26 calendar days. Direct temporary-opening/reassessment language is added to the current qualification; the initial two-month plan and South Ossetian 20:00 clock are not substituted for observed dates. Human disease control is directly attributed to the H1N1 precaution. No separate security rationale is inferred from border-service administration. The onset, resident reopening, ministry confirmation and conditional-authority accounts were directly inspected. Their scope and attribution remain distinct; source date conflicts are preserved. Enguri’s current binding remains unlocated with null coordinates. The phase does not gain geometry or a later unobserved period from its clearer reopening qualification.
